channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Astana Authorities Uncover Illegal Operations of Unlicensed Pawnshop
item.description: The Astana branch of the Financial Monitoring Agency has exposed the illegal activities of the 01market pawnshop, which operated multiple branches without a license. Suspects allegedly lent money by taking citizens' property as collateral. The illegal operation generated over 102 million tenge in profits.

item.title: Romit Biosphere Reserve Implements Digital Technologies for Nature Protection
item.description: A training seminar on using digital technologies for monitoring flora and fauna was held at the Romit Biosphere Reserve. Participants learned to use smartphones, SMART Patrol systems, and mobile apps for data collection in the field. The training also covered AI for species recognition.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches New 'One-Click' Tax Payment Service for Employers
item.description: Kazakhstan is launching a pilot project for 'one-click' tax payments from payroll starting November 17. The new service, available through the taxpayer's online cabinet, calculates and facilitates payments for income tax, pension contributions, and social deductions, offering an alternative to traditional tax reporting.

item.title: 14.5 km Road to Ala-Too Resort in Kyrgyzstan Undergoing Renovation
item.description: Construction is underway on a 14.5-kilometer section of the Boz-Uchuk – Shakhta – Jyrgalan road leading to the Ala-Too Resort ski resort in the Issyk-Kul region. "Kyrgyzavtodor" state enterprise reports that 62% of earthworks are complete, with pipes and retaining walls installed. The project aims to improve access and road safety.

item.title: Head of Information Security Department Appointed to Kazakhstan's Security Council Apparatus
item.description: By order of the Head of State, Baizhan Bolatuly Shalekenov has been appointed Head of the Information Security Department of the Security Council Apparatus. This appointment follows recent changes in national security leadership, including the replacement of the National Security Committee chairman.

item.title: IMF urges Uzbekistan to accelerate pension reform for economic and financial sector development
item.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has called on Uzbekistan to speed up its pension reform, identifying it as crucial for economic and financial sector advancement. While preparatory documents are ready, the reform remains in its early stages.

item.title: Uzbekistan Amends Labor Code to Prohibit Workplace Harassment
item.description: Uzbekistan has enacted a new law, signed by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, prohibiting workplace harassment. The amendment to the Labor Code introduces international standards, explicitly banning sexual harassment, including inappropriate comments, gestures, and touching. Employers are now obligated to ensure a harassment-free environment.

item.title: Kazakhstan Workers' Rights Explained: Overtime, Night Shifts, and Delayed Wages
item.description: A legal expert clarifies workers' rights in Kazakhstan regarding overtime pay, night shifts, and delayed wages. The explanation covers how to calculate additional pay for weekend and holiday work, penalties for late salary payments, and where to seek recourse if employers fail to meet their obligations.

item.title: Kazakh Minister Responds to Questions on Underground Madrasas Amidst 'Zikirshiler' Case
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of Education, Zhyldyz Suleimenova, addressed concerns about illegal religious educational institutions in light of the 'Zikirshiler' community case. She noted that only nine official madrasas operate in Kazakhstan and that certain theology-related specializations have been removed from the vocational education registry.

item.title: Solva Repays Bonds on AIX, Reports 4.1 Billion Tenge Profit in Nine Months
item.description: Solva Group has fully repaid its $10 million bond issuance on the Astana International Exchange (AIX) on time. The company reported a net profit of 4.1 billion tenge for the first nine months of 2026. Since August, under new management, Solva has paid out 27.7 billion tenge in obligations and attracted 14.2 billion tenge in new investments.

item.title: Kazakhstan May Ban Minors from Attending Evening Schools
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a ban on minors attending evening schools, according to Education Minister Zhyldyz Suleimenova. She stated that while evening schools for adults should continue, minors should receive education in general secondary institutions. The ministry notes that many minors listed as attending evening schools are not actually studying.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Replaces Head of National Security Committee Amid Corruption Scandal
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed Yermek Sagimbayev as chairman of the National Security Committee. Marat Irmenov, formerly deputy chairman, has been appointed as the new head of the intelligence agency. The reasons for the change were not specified, but the move follows recent arrests in a corruption probe involving state funds and the national railway company.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Path to Independence: The Introduction of the Tenge in 1993
item.description: Following the collapse of the USSR, Kazakhstan faced a choice: remain in Russia's ruble zone or introduce its own currency. Many former Soviet republics had already launched national currencies. Russia's monetary reform and the influx of old rubles led to hyperinflation in Kazakhstan. The National Bank of Kazakhstan developed a strategy for national currency introduction, aiming for economic stability.

item.title: Kazakhstan Police Detain Over 3,500 Individuals Without Permanent Residence
item.description: Between October 5 and November 5, Kazakhstan police apprehended over 3,500 individuals lacking permanent residence. Authorities registered nearly 42,000 migration law violations during this period, leading to administrative penalties for approximately 9,000 foreign nationals. The "Safe Home" operation involved inspecting over 576,000 residential properties.

item.title: ADB to Fund Up to $20 Million for Sustainable Transport Projects in Tajikistan
item.description: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved a financial mechanism of up to $20 million to prepare sustainable transport projects in Tajikistan. An initial initiative will modernize Dushanbe's public transport, including a dedicated bus lane on Somoni Avenue.

item.title: Tashkent Renovation Offers New City Apartments as Compensation for Residents
item.description: Residents in Tashkent whose homes are slated for renovation can now be offered apartments in New Tashkent as compensation. This new mechanism allows for compensation up to 1.5 times the assessed value of the previous property, potentially offering larger or multiple units.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Harvest Yields More Grain, Less Vegetables and Cotton in 2026
item.description: By late October 2026, Kyrgyzstan harvested 2.29 million tons of grain, a 27.8% increase from the previous year. Average grain yield rose to 37.3 centners per hectare. Wheat, barley, and corn yields saw significant increases, while vegetable and cotton harvests were lower.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Seeks Joint Projects within ECO Framework
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Foreign Minister attended the 30th meeting of the ECO Council of Foreign Ministers in Islamabad. Discussions focused on regional issues and cooperation in trade, economy, transport, energy, and humanitarian spheres. Kyrgyzstan expressed commitment to strengthening multilateral cooperation and utilizing ECO's potential for mutually beneficial partnerships and joint infrastructure projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan MPs Hold 155 Meetings to Explain President's Address
item.description: Over the past two weeks, Kazakhstan's Parliament members conducted 155 meetings across the country to explain President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address on "Urgent Tasks of Kazakhstan in a New Historical Era." Approximately 18,000 people participated, engaging in discussions on economic development, social modernization, and infrastructure renewal, including schools, hospitals, and roads.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Developing Loans and Deposits with Variable Interest Rates
item.description: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan plans to develop loans and deposits linked to the UZONIA interbank indicator, featuring variable interest rates. The initiative aims to improve the transmission of monetary policy changes. However, the regulator warns of potential risks from sharp rate fluctuations and suggests cautious implementation and training for banks in managing interest rate risks.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Increase Hero Mother Pension Supplement Fivefold
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to increase the pension supplement for mothers awarded the "Baatyr Ene" (Hero Mother) order from 1,000 to 5,000 soms. The bill was approved by a parliamentary committee. President has already signed a decree, with the increase effective from January 1, 2027. Over 30,000 women currently receive this supplement.

item.title: Third Candidate Secures Required Signatures for Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election
item.description: Aimen Kasenov has collected the minimum 30,000 voter signatures needed to register as a candidate for the upcoming presidential elections in Kyrgyzstan. He joins two other candidates who have also met the signature requirement. The signature collection period remains open until December 8th.

item.title: New Dairy Farm for 100 Cows Under Construction in Kyrgyzstan's Toktogul District
item.description: A new dairy farm for 100 cows is being built in the village of Komsomol, Toktogul District, Kyrgyzstan. The facility is 80% complete and aims to produce at least 2,000 liters of milk daily upon launch. The entrepreneur plans to import 100 pedigree cows from the Czech Republic in spring 2027.

item.title: Historical and Cultural Heritage Sites in Southern Kyrgyzstan to Be Nominated for UNESCO List
item.description: Several historical and cultural heritage sites in the Osh, Jalal-Abad, and Batken regions of Kyrgyzstan will be nominated for the UNESCO list under the Fergana and Syr Darya nominations. These include the Kulbes Khan mound (10th-12th centuries) and the Shah-Fazil mausoleum.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev and Singer Dimash Kudaibergen Named Among World's 500 Most Influential Muslims
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and singer Dimash Kudaibergen have been included in the 2027 edition of "The 500 Most Influential Muslims in the World" publication. The book highlights influential figures in politics, religion, science, culture, and sports.

item.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping to Attend APEC Summit in Shenzhen
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and deliver a speech in Shenzhen from November 18-19. The summit's theme is 'Building an Asia-Pacific Community for a Shared Future.' Xi will also attend the APEC Business Advisory Council dialogue and hold bilateral meetings with foreign leaders.

item.title: Man Arrested Attempting to Illegally Smuggle Gold Worth 488 Million Tenge to China
item.description: A resident of Almaty was apprehended at the Khorgos border crossing attempting to smuggle a large quantity of gold to China. Prosecutors revealed the man had taped the gold bars to his body to conceal them. The gold, weighing over 5.7 kilograms, was confiscated.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Strengthening Economic Partnership with ECO Member States
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Foreign Minister, Kairat Tursunkulov, attended the 30th ECO Council of Foreign Ministers meeting in Islamabad. He emphasized Kyrgyzstan's interest in enhancing cooperation, expanding trade, and implementing joint infrastructure and energy projects within the ECO framework.

item.title: Eurasian Energy War Disrupts Alternative Transportation Routes
item.description: The ongoing energy war in Eurasia is negatively impacting alternative transportation routes. This conflict is creating significant challenges for logistics and trade across the region.

item.title: Tajikistan Ministries Hold Meeting on Preventing Juvenile Delinquency Among Students
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministries of Education and Science and Internal Affairs held a meeting at Rasht Pedagogical Institute to prevent juvenile delinquency. The event focused on raising legal awareness and preventing youth involvement in illegal activities.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Launch New Rubber Plant in Atyrau Region by 2028
item.description: A new plant for butadiene rubber production with an annual capacity of 190,000 tons is set to be built in Kazakhstan's Atyrau region. Construction is underway, with site preparation completed and engineering surveys ongoing. The project, fully funded by Kazakhstan, was initially estimated at 414.52 billion tenge in February 2024.

item.title: Bishkek Suspends Licenses of 19 Construction Companies Amidst Unscrupulous Practices
item.description: Bishkek has suspended the licenses of 19 construction companies and revoked licenses for three others due to unscrupulous practices. Authorities are addressing 46 long-term unfinished construction projects in the capital, with a state directorate established for one company's projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan Education Minister Addresses Past Child Abuse Allegations
item.description: Education Minister Zhuldyz Suleimenova commented on allegations of child abuse involving preacher Ismatulla Abdugappar. She stated the issue is interdepartmental and requires further review, noting child protection units were established in 2026. The ministry can provide psychological support with the Ministry of Health for past incidents.

item.title: Tajikistan and Iran Agree to Expand Anti-Corruption Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan and Iran have agreed to develop a joint action plan to combat corruption for 2027-2028. The agreement was reached during a meeting between anti-corruption agency representatives in Dushanbe on November 13, 2026. Both sides emphasized strengthening bilateral cooperation, sharing best practices, and implementing joint initiatives.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Replaces Head of National Security Committee
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed Yermek Sagimbayev from his post as Chairman of Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB). Marat Irmenov has been appointed as the new chairman. Irmenov previously served as deputy chairman and has a background in national security operations and leadership roles.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans 15 MW Floating Solar Power Station at Hydro Plant
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to build a 15 MW floating solar power station at the GRES-5 hydroelectric facility in the Chuy region. The project, a collaboration between Chakan GRES and the Asian Development Bank (ADB), aims to expand solar generation on the reservoir. ADB is selecting a consultant for the project documentation.

item.title: Parental Responsibility Violations Increase in Kazakhstan
item.description: Cases of parental responsibility violations have significantly increased in Kazakhstan, with nearly 30,000 incidents recorded in 2026, up from 5,600 in 2020. The number of children found outdoors at night has also doubled. A deputy highlighted that over half of child deaths from falls and traffic accidents are linked to parental irresponsibility.

item.title: EADB: Kazakhstan's Manufacturing Sector Grows 9.3%, Tajikistan's Investments Up 44.9%
item.description: The Eurasian Development Bank reports Kazakhstan's GDP grew 4.5% in Jan-Oct, with manufacturing up 9.3%. Tajikistan's investments rose 44.9% in nine months, and its GDP grew 8.3%. Inflation accelerated in Belarus and Uzbekistan, while Russia's federal budget deficit was around 48 billion rubles in October.

item.title: Jordan Blocks Telegram Messenger to Enhance Digital Security and User Protection
item.description: Jordan has blocked the Telegram messenger as part of measures to improve digital security, protect users, and reduce threats and illegal activities. The Public Security Directorate stated the move aims to prevent the platform's misuse for cybercrime and spreading extremist content.

item.title: Almaty Resident Arrested Attempting to Smuggle Gold to China
item.description: A resident of Almaty was arrested at the Khorgos border crossing while attempting to smuggle approximately 5.76 kilograms of gold, valued at 488 million tenge, to China. The gold was found taped to his body. He has been found guilty of attempted economic smuggling.
